speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent, and I see you are bringing a newborn with respiratory distress. To begin my assessment, how long has this breathing difficulty been present, and was there any history of meconium aspiration or birth complications?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given the prematurity (32 weeks) and cesarean delivery, I need to clarify: was there any history of chorioamnionitis, and did the baby show signs of respiratory distress immediately after birth? Also, was there any blood staining of the amniotic fluid or vaginal bleeding during labor?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis in a 32-week preterm infant with a history of gestational diabetes is highly suggestive of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). To confirm this, I need to evaluate lung compliance and oxygenation status.

REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
